speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
text: asked the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (a) whether the Government's procurement process has criteria to encourage businesses to undertake environmental, social and governance (ESG) practices and, if so, what are they; (b) whether there is a national framework for businesses to track and measure the performance of businesses in ESG practices and, if not, whether there is consideration for one; and (c) what are the tax and non-tax incentives and schemes for businesses to undertake ESG practices, such as inclusive hiring of persons with special needs, rental of premises to conduct social businesses, capital investment improving ESG practices.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: In addition, events and functions organised by public sector agencies are to be held in venues with at least a Green Mark Certified rating, unless there are specific reasons why this is not possible.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: The criteria for the awarding of construction contracts for these building and other infrastructure projects include the use of productive construction methods which are typically also more sustainable.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: Besides procurement, there are various national frameworks in place for ESG practices in the private sector.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: The Ministry of Trade and Industry's Business Excellence programme, through the Singapore Quality Award (SQA) and the Singapore Quality Class (SQC) requires awarded organisations to have well-defined corporate governance systems to ensure business continuity and risk management, as well as accountability and transparency that are consistent with statutory and regulatory requirements.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: They are also required to have well-defined policies and programmes to contribute to the sustainable development of the community and environment which they operate in.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: So, ESG criteria are embedded within the SQA and SQC criteria.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: Enterprise Singapore also actively promotes the International Organization for Standardization standards related to ESG practices for the industry to adopt.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: We welcome other non-listed companies to consider and model their corporate practices on this guidance.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: In addition, there are various industry-led standards and certifications related to ESG practices, where companies are required to consider the impact of their decisions on their workers, customers, suppliers, community and the environment.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: The Urban Redevelopment Authority provides additional bonus gross floor area when commercial building owners set aside space for community and sports use.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: New and existing social enterprises benefit from Government grants when starting up or expanding their operations.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: So, these are just examples of the various incentive programmes that we have in place.

speaker: The Second Minister for Finance (Mr Lawrence Wong) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
text: The Government will continue to review these schemes and encourage firms and employees to make full use of them to strengthen their ESG practices.
